newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela allows oilspill captain trip home.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela allows oilspill captain trip home.

text.p: The Greek captain of the Nissos Amorgos oil tanker, detained without charge for five months since his ship spilled part of its cargo off the Venezuelan coast, was allowed a trip home on Saturday, a diplomat said on Monday.

Captain Konstantino Spyropoulos has been under arrest since February 28 when the Greek-flagged ship, under the command of a Venezuelan pilot, struck bottom in Lake Maracaibo channel and spilled 25,000 barrels of crude oil.

"He is not free. He has a permit to travel to Greece for 30 days. He has to be back here on September 14. We managed to get him the permit with my guarantee and that of his lawyer," said Konstantin Hadjis, Greek consul to Venezuela in Maracaibo.
The guarantees cost 100,000 bolivars ($200), he added.
Pollution is a criminal offence in Venezuela and Spiropoulos must be present to hear the charges against him after the courts come back from summer recess on September 15.
The detention has brought criticism from international tanker organisation Intertanko which said Venezuela was violating his human rights.
Although not in jail, Spyropoulos had been forbidden from leaving the western Zulia state and had to report to authorities every 25 days.
The courts released the tanker itself on July 21.

The Nissos Amorgos was the first of three tankers to run aground in the same spot bringing charges that the channel, Venezuela's main oil export route, was poorly maintained. Carlos Punar Abreu, president of the National Dredging Institute (INC), was sacked in March.

The same Venezuelan court is also holding the captain of the Plate Princess, a Maltese-flagged tanker which spilled 20 barrels of crude in the Lake Maracaibo on May 29. This ship was released on July 19.
